summary: A generated answer presented so the reader can check it: the text, what it was drawn from, and how far to trust it.
useWhen: an answer is generated from sources the user could go and read
the answer will be acted on — a policy question, a number, a recommendation
the answer may be wrong in ways that are not visible from the text alone
structure: The answer in a StreamingText, with inline Citation markers at the claims they support — not gathered at the end.
A CitationList below the answer, one CitationListItem per source, numbered to match the inline markers.
A ConfidenceIndicator beside the answer, with `basis` saying what the level is derived from.
An Alert only when the answer is degraded — sources unavailable, knowledge stale, question outside scope.

loading.must: Stream the text with `isStreaming` and `minLines` set. Render no ConfidenceIndicator and no CitationList until the answer is complete.
loading.why: a confidence level attached to half an answer is a claim about text that does not exist yet, and citations that appear one by one move the reader's place on every token

empty.must: When there is no answer — no sources matched, the question was out of scope — say that in words and render neither an empty CitationList nor a ConfidenceIndicator.
empty.why: an answer with no sources and no confidence shown reads as a confident answer, which is the opposite of what an empty result means

error.must: Keep whatever text arrived, mark it plainly as incomplete with an Alert of `intent="warning"`, and drop the ConfidenceIndicator entirely.
error.why: a truncated answer that keeps its confidence badge is rated on evidence it never finished reading

partial.must: When some sources were unreachable, cite the ones that were, lower the `level`, and name the gap in `basis` — "3 of 7 sources; 4 unavailable".
partial.why: an answer built on half its evidence looks identical to one built on all of it, and `basis` is the only place that difference can be stated

requires: an `index` on every Citation that matches its CitationListItem — the number is how a screen-reader user connects the two
a `basis` on ConfidenceIndicator, which the component requires and which must describe evidence, not feeling
a `label` on StreamingText when no visible heading precedes the answer
notes: A Citation with no `href` renders as a note, not a dead link. Pass `href` only when the source is genuinely reachable by the reader.
Citation's accessible name is `Source <index>: <source>`, so the source string should name the document, not say "link" or "here".
StreamingText is not a live region. Announcing that the answer finished is the caller's decision — a thread with ten answers on screen does not want ten announcements.

antiPatterns.why: the number is not calibrated against anything, and a false precision is trusted more than the vague statement it replaced

antiPatterns.dont: citations gathered only at the end of the answer
antiPatterns.why: the reader cannot tell which claim each source supports, so the list documents that sources exist rather than what they establish

antiPatterns.dont: citing a source the reader cannot open
antiPatterns.why: an unreachable citation is decoration that raises trust without supplying any way to check it

antiPatterns.dont: a confidence level derived from the model's own token probabilities and presented as certainty about the world
antiPatterns.why: fluency and correctness are different quantities, and only one of them is being measured

antiPatterns.dont: hiding the sources behind a disclosure that defaults closed
antiPatterns.why: evidence that takes a click to reach is evidence nobody checks
